hints.title: Spanning Tree Cycle Creation Obstacle
hints.text: Adding an edge between vertices that are already connected in a spanning tree creates a cycle. How can you keep track of connected groups as you inspect edges one by one to pinpoint the first edge that connects an already connected component?

hints.title: Canonical Root Cycle Invariant
hints.text: In a tree, adding an edge between two vertices with the same canonical representative creates a cycle. That edge is redundant.

hints.title: Disjoint Set Union Procedure
hints.text: Initialize each vertex as its own parent. For each edge, find the canonical roots of both endpoints. If both roots are identical, the current edge forms a cycle and is the answer. Otherwise, union the two components by attaching one root to the other.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of vertices / edges (3 <= N <= 1000)
complexity.notes: Path compression in Disjoint Set Union ensures near constant time per edge inspection.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Rebuilding and searching the entire graph with DFS per edge takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Union-find parent array provides O(N) space and nearly O(N) overall execution time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Path compression implementation, recognizing tree cycle property, returning the redundant edge in order of appearance.
